gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-noto-sans-th: Wobbly and playful, Jelly Crazies draws its letters like bent wire. Noto Sans Thaana follows with wide channels into each counter and big open lowercase forms, so the heading gets its laugh and the text stays approachable.
Fat, bouncy, nearly sealed shut. Jelly Crazies closes its bowls while Noto Sans Thai swells its lowercase like glass beads and leaves the rounds open, which is the whole charm of the pairing.

Jelly Crazies keeps every curve at full thickness, with bowls that nearly seal shut and a wobbly, playful bounce. Noto Sans Thai Looped carries on in tall, bold-looking lowercase with spacious gaps at its curve ends, so the eye moves along comfortably.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-noto-sans-ti: Noto Sans Tifinagh keeps its rounded letters open and inviting. Jelly Crazies brings a wobbly, monoweight stroke up top, and the body's inflated-looking bowls fill the line while the closed heading shapes stay playful against them.

Playful and wobbly, Jelly Crazies hits with a sign-painter's-stencil flatness and bowls nearly shut. Noto Sans Tirhuta does the opposite job, cutting its terminals back to leave a big gap and letting a dominant x-height carry the reading.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-noto-sans-ug: Noto Sans Ugaritic has hardly any step between x-height and cap height, with open mouths like an unjoined chalk arc. Jelly Crazies, wobbly and flat in stroke, makes the more playful contrast, and that difference is the strongest thing here.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-noto-sans-va: Chunky, wobbly and a bit goofy up top. Jelly Crazies closes its letters tight, and Noto Sans Vai gives generous space between curve ends and the stem, so its words settle into solid blocks beneath.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-noto-sans-vi: Wobbly, closed-up and cheerful, Jelly Crazies goes first. Noto Sans Vithkuqi has open throats on a, c, e and s and barely any step from capital to lowercase, so give the body some extra size and it opens up nicely.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-noto-sans-wa: Noto Sans Wancho reads thick and hulking, like chalk pressed hard. Give that body a little extra size and its wide-gapped e breathes, while Jelly Crazies keeps a ballpoint-thin wobble up top.

Bent tubing in one gauge, wobbly and playful. Noto Sans Warang Citi turns that into solid blocks of words with wide channels into each counter, and its clean openness against the heading's closed bowls is the strongest thing here.
